papers.title: Sequential Meridian Based Acupuncture Combined With Standard Rehabilitation After Surgery for Severe Cubital Tunnel Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Ding L, Zhang Q, Si Y, Zhou H, Chen Z, Qu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the efficacy of sequential meridian-based acupuncture combined with standard rehabilitation in patients after surgery for severe cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS).
In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 40 patients with severe CuTS who underwent ulnar nerve decompression with subfascial anterior transposition combined with supercharged end-to-side nerve transfers (the pronator quadratus branch and the abductor digiti minimi branch to the deep branch of the ulnar nerve) were randomly assigned to a sequential acupuncture group and a standard rehabilitation group (n=20). The standard rehabilitation group received neurotrophic medication and progressive rehabilitation training; the sequential acupuncture group additionally received staged meridian-based acupuncture (the Small Intestine Meridian and the Triple Energizer Meridian were primarily selected during postoperative months 0 to 3, supplemented by the Large Intestine Meridian thereafter, combining filiform-needle acupuncture and electroacupuncture). Motor nerve conduction velocity (MCV), sensory nerve conduction velocity (SCV), lateral pinch strength ratio, ring-finger grip strength ratio, 2-point discrimination (2PD), DASH score, EQ-5D-5L score, and VAS score were assessed preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively.
Thirty-seven patients completed follow-up (18 in the sequential acupuncture group and 19 in the standard rehabilitation group; overall dropout rate 7.5%), with no acupuncture-related adverse events. Baseline characteristics were balanced between the 2 groups (P>0.05). Beginning at 3 months postoperatively, improvements in MCV, lateral pinch strength ratio, ring-finger grip strength ratio, DASH score, and EQ-5D-5L score were greater in the sequential acupuncture group than in the standard rehabilitation group (P<0.05), with between-group differences widening at 6 months (P<0.01). Group×time interactions were significant for these 6 indicators (P<0.001), and between-group differences in improvement magnitude reached large effect sizes (MCV: MD=5.80 m/s, 95% CI: 4.70-6.90; SCV: MD=4.65 m/s, 95% CI: 3.30-6.01; lateral pinch strength ratio: d=2.165; ring-finger grip strength ratio: d=2.321). No significant between-group differences were observed in ring-finger or little-finger 2PD or in VAS score at any time point (P>0.05).
Sequential meridian-based acupuncture combined with standard rehabilitation accelerates postoperative electrophysiological and intrinsic hand muscle recovery and improves upper-limb function and quality of life in patients with severe CuTS. The therapeutic advantage emerges during postoperative months 3 to 6, the critical window of nerve regeneration, with a favorable safety profile.
papers.title_ko: 중증 주관증후군 수술 후 표준 재활에 순차적 경락 기반 침을 병행한 무작위대조시험

summary.question: 수술 후 중증 주관증후군 환자에서 순차적 경락 기반 침이 표준 재활만 시행할 때보다 회복을 더 개선하는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 전향적 무작위대조시험에서 수술 후 환자를 순차적 침군과 표준 재활군으로 배정해, 전기침을 포함한 단계적 경락 침 치료를 표준 재활에 추가하고 6개월까지 기능과 신경생리 지표를 비교했다.
summary.results: 순차적 침군은 수술 3~6개월부터 운동·감각 신경전도, 손 기능 일부, DASH 및 EQ-5D-5L가 더 크게 호전되었고, 2점 식별과 통증은 두 군 차이가 없었으며 침 관련 이상반응은 없었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 중증 주관증후군 수술 후 재활에 경락 기반 침을 병행하면 회복 속도와 일부 기능지표 개선이 관찰되었으나, 단일 연구 결과이므로 임상 적용은 근거 축적을 함께 보아야 한다.
summary.limitations: 표본이 작고 단일 연구이며, 감각 및 통증 지표에서는 추가 이점이 확인되지 않았다.

papers.title: Neuropeptides in Immunometabolism and Neuroinflammation: Insights from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.authors: Wu CH, Cheng CF, Nguyen TKN, Su LY, Lee MC, Chuang WC
papers.abstract: Neuropeptides are small bioactive peptides secreted by neurons and immune cells that serve as critical messengers in both central and peripheral systems. Recent studies have identified key neuropeptides-such as Substance P (SP), Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide (VIP), Neuropeptide Y (NPY), and Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide (CGRP)-as pivotal regulators of immunometabolism and neuroinflammation. These peptides influence macrophage polarization, T cell differentiation, cytokine production, and neuroimmune crosstalk, linking chronic inflammation to conditions such as obesity, diabetes, autoimmunity, and neurodegeneration. This review synthesizes emerging evidence on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) interventions-including herbal formulas, single herbs, bioactive compounds, and acupuncture-that modulate neuropeptide signaling via NF-κB, MAPK, and Nrf2 pathways. These mechanisms contribute to analgesia, emotional stabilization, metabolic regulation, and neuroprotection. The article further presents a modular framework connecting representative Chinese medicinal substances to specific neuropeptides and physiological functions, offering a translational foundation for neuropeptide-targeted therapies and integrative precision health strategies.

summary.question: 전통중의학 중재가 면역대사와 신경염증에 관여하는 신경펩타이드 조절과 어떤 관련이 있는지 검토한 논문이다.
summary.methods: 주요 신경펩타이드와 전통중의학의 약재·한약복합처방·단일약재·생약성분·침술이 관련 경로를 조절하는 근거를 종합한 서술적 समीक्षा이다.
summary.results: SP, VIP, NPY, CGRP와 같은 신경펩타이드는 면역대사와 신경염증의 핵심 조절자로 제시되었고, 전통중의학 중재는 NF-κB, MAPK, Nrf2 경로를 통해 이를 조절하는 것으로 요약되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 한의학적 중재가 신경펩타이드-면역염증 축과 연결될 가능성을 보여주지만, 임상 적용 전에는 개별 중재의 근거 수준과 대상 질환별 근거를 따로 확인해야 한다.

papers.title: Baihe Zhimu Decoction ameliorates anxious depression via PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway-mediated neuroprotection and inhibition of hippocampal neuronal apoptosis.
papers.authors: Han Y, He K, Yang H, Dai J, Chen R, Liu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Anxious depression involves severe emotional dysregulation with a high risk of relapse and suicide. Although the classical Traditional Chinese Medicine formula Baihe Zhimu Decoction (BZD) is widely used for affective disorders, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
In this study, the chemical constituents of BZD were first identified using UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, followed by a maximum-dose safety evaluation. The therapeutic effects of BZD were then investigated in an anxious-depression mouse model induced by chronic restraint stress (CRS) combined with corticosterone (CORT) administration. Behavioral assessments, including the open field test (OFT), elevated plus maze (EPM), sucrose preference test (SPT), and forced swim test (FST), were performed, together with histopathological examination of hippocampal tissues. Network pharmacology was employed to analyze the relationships between active compounds and potential targets and to predict related signaling pathways. Subsequently, western blot analysis, immunofluorescence staining, Hoechst staining, and flow cytometry, combined with pathway-specific inhibitors, were used to examine the involvement of the signaling pathway in hippocampal tissues and primary hippocampal neurons.
Forty-one constituents were identified in BZD. In vivo results showed that BZD significantly alleviated hippocampal pathological injury and improved anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in stressed mice. Network pharmacology analysis identified 19 active compounds and 622 potential targets, highlighting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Mechanistically, BZD activated this pathway and protected against neuronal injury, while these effects were attenuated by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002.
BZD exerts potent neuroprotective and therapeutic effects against anxious depression, primarily driven by activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and preserving hippocampal neuronal integrity.

papers.title: Elucidating the multi-target therapeutic mechanism of Kangtai decoction in lung cancer through integrated network pharmacology and molecular docking.
papers.journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
papers.authors: Niu J, Yang Y, Hui Y, Feng C
papers.abstract:
Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with a high incidence and limited effective treatments, the main focus being on symptom management and tumor control. Kangtai decoction (KTD), a traditional Chinese medicine, has shown promising results in alleviating lung cancer symptoms and improving quality of life in China, though its precise mechanism of action remains unclear.
This study employed a network pharmacology-based approach, complemented by molecular docking, to identify the bioactive components, key targets, and potential pharmacological mechanisms of KTD against lung cancer.
Bioactive components and drug targets of KTD, along with targets related to lung cancer, were collected from public databases. Bioinformatics analyses, including protein-protein interaction (PPI), gene ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses, were conducted to identify core targets, bioactive components, and signaling pathways. Molecular docking was then performed to predict the binding between active compounds and core targets.
A total of 145 effective components of KTD for treating lung cancer were screened, along with 113 common targets between KTD and lung cancer. Bioinformatics analysis and molecular docking indicated that in the treatment of lung cancer with KTD, neocryptotanshinone II was the most significant bioactive compound, IL1B was the most pivotal target, and the IL-17 signaling pathway was the most critical pathway.
KTD is effective in the treatment of lung cancer, possibly because of the binding of its active components to key therapeutic targets involved in lung cancer.

papers.title: Acupuncture and Moxibustion for Neck Pain: A Clinical Practice Guideline.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Yin Z, Sun X, Liang F, Zhao J, Zhu L et al.
papers.abstract:
Neck pain (NP) is a leading cause of disability worldwide. Pharmacological treatments often provide limited benefits and may be associated with adverse effects, highlighting the need for effective non-pharmacological options.
To develop evidence-based recommendations on the effectiveness, safety, and clinical implementation of acupuncture and/or moxibustion for adults with NP.
This guideline was developed in accordance with the Reporting Items for practice Guidelines in HealThcare (RIGHT) statement for acupuncture and the BMJ Rapid Recommendations process. Recommendations were informed by a systematic review of 88 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 10,172 participants. Evidence certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE), and recommendations were formulated through an evidence-to-decision framework and multidisciplinary consensus.
The guideline proposed five recommendations: (1) acupuncture and/or moxibustion is suggested rather than no such treatment (weak recommendation, moderate-certainty); (2) acupuncture and/or moxibustion may be considered for patients with moderate-to-severe pain or prolonged symptoms (weak recommendation, low-certainty); (3) adding acupuncture and/or moxibustion to usual care is suggested rather than usual care alone (weak recommendation, low-certainty); (4) an initial 3-4-week course, using 5-10 acupoints/session and 3-5 sessions/week, may serve as a reference regimen (weak recommendation, low-certainty); and (5) electroacupuncture may be preferentially considered for pain relief and functional improvement, whereas manual acupuncture, warm needling, and moxibustion may be alternatives (weak recommendation, low-certainty). Adverse events were generally mild and self-limiting.
Acupuncture and/or moxibustion may be reasonable and safe non-pharmacological options for adults with NP. Clinical use should be guided by shared decision-making that considers symptom severity, disease duration, treatment goals, patient preferences, accessibility, and practitioner expertise.

papers.title: Gardenia jasminoides Ellis 70% ethanolic fraction alleviates hyperuricemia by upregulating PPARγ and modulating its downstream urate transporters and anti-inflammatory pathways.
papers.authors: Li R, Chen G, Li Y, Liu H, Huang L, Yang C et al.
papers.abstract:
Gardenia jasminoides Ellis (GJE) is a traditional Chinese medicine widely used for metabolic disorders. However, its efficacy against hyperuricemia, the responsible active fraction, and the underlying mechanisms of its effect remains to be clarified.
To investigate the material basis and urate-lowering activity of the 70% ethanolic fraction of GJE (GJE70), and to elucidate its molecular mechanism.
UPLC-Q-TOF-MS characterized the chemical composition of GJE70. Hyperuricemia was induced in rats by potassium oxonate and yeast extract. Serum and urinary uric acid, uric acid clearance, renal function, and histopathology were assessed for anti-hyperuricemia efficacy and urate excretion. Hepatic function and histology were examined for safety. To explore mechanisms, kidney transcriptomics and metabolomics were performed; molecular docking predicted compound-target binding, which was validated by IF, WB, qRT-PCR and rescue experiments in HK-2 cells.
UPLC-Q-TOF-MS identified 18 major compounds in GJE70, with crocins predominant. In hyperuricemia rats, GJE70 significantly reduced serum uric acid and increased urinary uric acid excretion and clearance, indicating enhanced renal urate elimination. Renal function and histopathology showed alleviated renal injury without obvious hepatotoxicity, with normal liver enzymes and histology. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that GJE70 mainly modulated PPAR signaling pathways. Molecular docking and MD Analysis demonstrated strong binding affinities of compounds to PPARγ. Subsequent IF, WB, and qRT-PCR confirmed that GJE70 upregulated PPARγ expression and its downstream urate transporters (ABCG2, OAT1, and OAT3), and suppressed NF-κB signaling levels. In HK-2 cells, GJE70 reduced supernatant uric acid, upregulated ABCG2/OAT1/OAT3, and inhibited NF-κB activation; GW9662 attenuated these effects, confirming PPARγ dependence.
GJE70 exerts potent urate-lowering and renoprotective effects via PPARγ-mediated regulation of urate transporters and anti-inflammatory pathways, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for hyperuricemia.

papers.title: Oxysophocarpine attenuates acute liver injury by targeting FBP1 to suppress ferroptosis and enhance cellular resilience via the PPARα-GPX4 axis.
papers.authors: Shi J, Liu Y, Wang R, Li X, Jiang Y, Yu J et al.
papers.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a life-threatening clinical condition with limited therapeutic options. Through network pharmacology screening, we identified oxysophocarpine (OSC), a natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, as a potent reactive oxygen species-scavenging agent. In LPS/D-GalN-induced ALI models, OSC administration dose-dependently improved survival, attenuated histopathological damage, reduced serum transaminase levels and inflammatory cytokines, and enhanced antioxidant capacity. Notably, we report for the first time that OSC directly bound to fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (FBP1) and modulated its interaction with peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα), leading to upregulated glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) expression and subsequent inhibition of ferroptosis, apoptosis, and endoplasmic reticulum stress. Collectively, this study reveals a multidimensional protective mechanism of OSC against ALI centered on FBP1 targeting, integrating anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-cell death activities, thereby providing a rationale for developing OSC as a promising natural product-based therapy for ALI.

papers.title: Ejiao (Asini Corii Colla) promotes thin endometrium repair via upregulation of the SDF-1/CXCR4 signalling axis in a mouse model.
papers.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
papers.authors: Tan M, Wei H, Wei D, Lai T, Xiao J
papers.abstract:
Thin endometrium (TE) severely impairs embryo implantation and pregnancy outcomes in reproductive medicine, while first-line oestrogen-based therapy has marked limitations including receptor insensitivity and systemic side effects. Ejiao (Asini Corii Colla), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine tonic, is widely used for gynecological disorders, yet its mechanism in endometrial regeneration remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effect of Ejiao on TE and its regulation of the SDF-1/CXCR4 signalling axis.
A TE mouse model was established via intrauterine infusion of 95% ethanol in female C57BL/6J mice. Mice were randomly divided into 4 groups (n = 6 per group): sham operation control group, TE model group, oestradiol positive control group (0.04 mg/kg/d), and Ejiao intervention group (0.2 g/kg/d), with 4 weeks of daily gavage intervention. Oestrous cycle stability was verified by vaginal smears, endometrial morphology was evaluated by HE staining, and SDF-1/CXCR4 mRNA expression in uterine tissues was detected by qPCR.
All mice maintained stable oestrous cycling throughout the experiment. Ejiao treatment markedly restored endometrial thickness and glandular density in TE mice, with a superior reparative effect to oestradiol, and significantly upregulated the mRNA expression of SDF-1 and CXCR4 in uterine tissue (P < 0.05 vs. model and oestradiol groups).
Ejiao effectively promotes endometrial regeneration in TE mice via upregulating the SDF-1/CXCR4 signalling axis, providing preclinical mechanistic evidence for its clinical application in TE treatment.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture synergizes with anti-ferroptosis bioelectrical niche remodeling to promote spinal cord regeneration.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Mo Y, Yan B, Wang X, Wu P, Wu Y et al.
papers.abstract: Severe spinal cord injury (SCI) frequently causes persistent neurological deficits, and its repair is constrained by multiple pathological factors including deterioration of the microenvironment following secondary injury, massive neuronal loss, interruption of electrical signal conduction, and insufficient endogenous regenerative capacity. Although electroacupuncture (EA) participates in the rehabilitation of SCI by regulating inflammatory responses and promoting the secretion of neurotrophic factors, standalone EA therapy can hardly fully reverse oxidative stress, ferroptosis and neural circuit destruction following severe SCI. Accordingly, this study constructs a conductive anti-ferroptosis hydrogel system (HBP@BMSCs), which utilizes dopamine-grafted hyaluronic acid (HADA) as the bionic matrix, baicalin-polypyrrole (BA-PPy) as the functional component, and is loaded with bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). This hydrogel system is combined with EA for the repair of severe SCI. The results demonstrate that the HBP hydrogel exhibits favorable cytocompatibility, which can support the survival of BMSCs and maintain their typical mesenchymal stem cell phenotype. In vitro experiments demonstrate that HBP hydrogel effectively alleviates TBHP-induced oxidative stress injury and Erastin-induced ferroptosis-related injury, and exerts a protective effect on BMSCs and PC12 cells. In vivo experiments further confirmed that the combination therapy of HBP@BMSCs with EA significantly downregulated the expression levels of 4HNE, COX2, NOX2, FTH, FTL and TFR after SCI, and restored the expression levels of XCT, GPX4, SOD1 and FPN, thereby alleviating ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, iron overload and ferroptosis. With the alleviation of oxidative stress and ferroptosis-related secondary damage, the combination therapy further downregulates the expression of Bax and C-caspase3, upregulates Bcl-2 levels, and significantly inhibits neuronal apoptosis. In addition, the BA-PPy conductive network can synergize with EA to enhance electrical stimulation conduction, upregulate NGF/NGFR and BDNF neurotrophic signaling pathways, and promote the neural lineage differentiation of BMSCs, axon regeneration, corticospinal tract (CST) remodeling, and the recovery of motor function. In conclusion, HBP@BMSCs combined with EA exerts multiple synergistic effects including microenvironment remodeling, anti-ferroptosis protection, stem cell delivery and electroactive neural regeneration, providing a comprehensive therapeutic strategy with translational potential for severe SCI repair.

papers.title: Comprehensive Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies Potential Biomarkers and Underlying Mechanisms of Acupuncture in Treating Peripheral Facial Paralysis.
papers.authors: Li X, Li Y, Zou X, Liu J, Yin R, Wei Q et al.
papers.abstract: Peripheral facial palsy (PFP) is a common neurological disorder. Acupuncture is an effective therapeutic intervention, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. To evaluate the clinical efficacy of acupuncture for PFP and to identify differentially expressed RNAs and associated pathways via whole transcriptome analysis, thereby revealing potential molecular mechanisms. Clinical efficacy was assessed using the House-Brackmann (HB) scale, Facial Disability Index (FDI), and comprehensive traditional Chinese medicine efficacy criteria. Peripheral blood samples were collected from patients before and after acupuncture treatment. Differentially expressed circRNAs, lncRNAs, miRNAs, and mRNAs were screened through whole transcriptome sequencing. Bioinformatics analyses were employed to construct a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network and perform Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analyses. Acupuncture significantly improved clinical scores post-treatment. A total of 1625 differentially expressed mRNAs (1153 up-, 472 down-regulated), 715 lncRNAs (321 up-, 394 down-regulated), 85 circRNAs (56 up-, 29 down-regulated), and 253 miRNAs (141 up-, 112 down-regulated) were identified. The ceRNA network revealed that non-coding RNAs competitively bind key miRNA molecules, forming two distinct and independent regulatory axes that precisely modulate downstream target genes. KEGG enrichment analysis of core molecular targets indicated significant involvement in the Olfactory transduction and JAK-STAT signaling pathways. Acupuncture may exert its therapeutic effect on PFP by modulating the ceRNA network, alongside the Olfactory transduction and JAK-STAT signaling pathways, synergistically promoting nerve regeneration and suppressing neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Terpenes and terpenoids modulating TRPV channels in diabetes: role in fibrosis and inflammatory signaling.
papers.authors: Awate SA, Kaur G
papers.abstract: Transient receptor potential vanilloid (TRPV) channels are non-selective cation channels that mediate thermosensation, nociception, osmotic balance, and metabolic regulation. In diabetes, altered TRPV channel expression and decreased calcium influx key pathways modulates, include NF-κB, AMPK, and TGF-β, promoting extracellular matrix accumulation and fibrotic remodelling. The limited availability of pathway specific interventions highlights TRPV channels as potential therapeutic target in diabetes. Recently, natural phytoconstituents have shown to exhibit TRPV channel modulating properties. Studies also highlights the potential of terpenes and terpenoids to inhibit NF-κB mediated inflammation, and activate AMPK-promoted metabolic homeostasis, mitigating diabetes-associated tissue damage. Preclinical studies have explored major terpenoids such as d-limonene, p-cymene and carvacrol in diabetic models. These compounds have been reported to improve glucose tolerance and alter the blood glucose levels via different molecular mechanisms. Clinically, there are limited evidences reporting terpenoids in the metabolic syndrome and TRPV modulation. Example, Astaxanthin, a tetraterpenoid has multiple human trials in type 2 diabetes, reducing diabetic biomarkers like SIRT1, HbA1c, and fasting glucose. This review summarizes current evidence on terpenes and terpenoids in diabetes with their reported and proposed interactions with TRPV1, TRPV4 with particular emphasis on their potential links to oxidative stress, NF-κB-mediated inflammation, TGF-β-associated fibrosis, and metabolic signaling. By distinguishing experimentally supported TRPV modulation with mechanistic associations and which require further validation, this review provides an integrated framework for understanding potential contribution of terpenoid-TRPV interactions to diabetes progression and its inflammatory and fibrotic complications, while highlighting key gaps for future experimental and translational investigation.

papers.title: Ginseng alleviates fatigue by inhibiting autophagy via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway.
papers.authors: Liu H, Xiong R, Zhang S, Zhang P, Wang L, Wang Q et al.
papers.abstract:
Panax ginseng C. A. Mey. (PG) is a commonly used traditional Chinese medicine to relieve fatigue-related symptoms. However, the underlying mechanisms by which PG alleviates fatigue are still not fully understood. This study aims to elucidate the anti-fatigue mechanism of PG in a hyperammonemia induced fatigue mouse model.
The therapeutic effects of PG on hyperammonemia-induced fatigue mice were evaluated using behavioral assessments, including rotarod, open field, grip strength, and tail suspension tests, along with serum biochemical analysis and hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining. To investigate the molecular mechanisms, an integrated approach combining transcriptomics, proteomics, network pharmacology, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and Western blot was employed.
PG significantly enhanced the exercise tolerance of hyperammonemia-induced fatigue mice, ameliorated skeletal muscle fiber atrophy, and restored the serum ammonia, creatine kinase, blood urea nitrogen, lactate dehydrogenase, and blood glucose levels. Comprehensive analysis of transcriptomics, proteomics and network pharmacology indicated that the mechanism of anti-fatigue of PG may be mediated by regulating autophagy via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. In addition, immunohistochemistry, Western blot, and immunofluorescence analysis confirmed that PG protected against fatigue by activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway to restore dysregulated autophagy in skeletal muscle under hyperammonemia conditions.
PG may alleviate fatigue by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and restoring the protein balance within skeletal muscle.

papers.title: Prevalence and independent influencing factors of moderate-to-severe cancer-related fatigue (CRF) and its association with Buzhong-Yiqi (BZYQ) use among patients with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma (LACSCC): a retrospective observational study using propensity-score weighting (PSW) logistic regression model.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.authors: Li C, Luo Z, Tian L, Deng W, Pang Q, Bentley GT et al.
papers.abstract:
Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a debilitating syndrome in cervical cancer patients, resistant to conventional bedrest. This study analyzed CRF drivers and observed the real-world correlation of the Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulation, Buzhong Yiqi, in the incidence of the moderate-to-severe CRF patients with stage IIB-IVA cervical carcinoma.
This was a retrospective observational study conducted at Chengdu Xinjin District People's Hospital and Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital. According to inclusion and exclusion criteria, we enrolled patients diagnosed with stage IIB-IVA cervical squamous carcinoma (FIGO 2018 criteria). We identified factors influencing CRF severity using Electronic Medical Records and patient questionnaires. The prevalence of CRF was estimated among patients diagnosed with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma (LACSCC). According to the univariate and multivariate analysis, we want to find the independent influencing factors of moderate-to-severe CRF. Independent sample t-tests and Chi-squared tests were performed to assess differences in symptom scores between BZYQ (Buzhong-Yiqi)-treated and non BZYQ-treated groups. A propensity score-weighted(PSW) logistic regression model was employed to evaluate the association between the real-world BZYQ treatment and the risk of moderate-to-severe CRF.
We enrolled 144 patients diagnosed with stage IIB-IVA cervical squamous carcinoma (FIGO 2018 criteria) who underwent chemoradiation, chemotherapy alone, radiation therapy alone, targeting therapy or no anticancer treatment. Among them, 50% had moderate-to-severe CRF. Independent factors significantly influencing the incidence of moderate-to-severe CRF included disease stage (P = 0.001), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG-PS) (P = 0.003), cancer pain (P < 0.001), anemia (P < 0.001), poor appetite (P < 0.001), proactive clinician attention (P = 0.042) and BZYQ treatment (P = 0.001). After propensity-score weighting, the BZYQ-treatment group exhibited a 68.3% reduction in the odds of moderate to severe CRF (OR = 0.317; P < 0.001).
CRF is a complex, multifactorial syndrome driven by tumor burden, synergistic symptoms, and quality of supportive care. Among patients with LACSCC, CRF is common. In clinical practice, CRF should be included in routine screening to achieve early identification and early intervention. Throughout the course of diagnosis and treatment, long-term dynamic assessment and timely interventions should be implemented for modifiable risk factors such as cancer-related pain, anemia and poor appetite, so as to reduce the risk and severity of CRF. Meanwhile, clinicians should actively attend to patients' complaints of fatigue and strengthen awareness for the identification and standardized management of this symptom. This real-world observational study suggests that BZYQ treatment is correlated with the decreased incidence of moderate-to-severe CRF, providing preliminary clues for further exploring its application value in CRF management.

summary.methods: FIGO 2018 기준의 IIB-IVA 자궁경부 편평세포암 환자를 대상으로 전자의무기록과 설문을 활용한 후향적 관찰연구로, 다변량 분석과 성향점수 가중 로지스틱 회귀를 시행했다.
summary.results: 전체 144명 중 50%가 중등도-중증 피로를 보였고, 병기·ECOG-PS·암성 통증·빈혈·식욕저하·의료진의 적극적 관심과 보중익기탕 치료가 관련 요인으로 나타났으며, 보중익기탕군은 성향점수 가중 후 중등도-중증 피로의 오즈가 낮았다(OR 0.317).
summary.clinical_takeaway: 국소 진행 자궁경부암에서 피로는 흔하며 통증, 빈혈, 식욕저하 같은 조절 가능한 요인과 함께 표준화된 선별과 추적이 필요하고, 보중익기탕은 관찰연구 수준의 예비 신호로만 해석하는 것이 적절하다.
summary.limitations: 후향적 단일 시기 관찰연구로 인과성을 확정할 수 없고, 보중익기탕 효과는 잔여 교란의 영향을 받을 수 있다.

pico.p: IIB-IVA 국소 진행 자궁경부 편평세포암 환자
pico.o: 중등도-중증 암 관련 피로의 유병률 및 발생 오즈

papers.title: Deciphering the mechanisms of resveratrol in knee osteoarthritis treatment: insights from bioinformatics and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Huang C, Ye X, Liu X, Liu F, Li Y, Chen X et al.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is the most prevalent chronic joint disorder in orthopedics, with its underlying pathogenic genes and effective treatment methods remaining unclear. Resveratrol (RES), a potent bioactive natural polyphenol, has been shown to effectively alleviate KOA; however, its complex regulatory mechanisms require further investigation. This research seeks to clarify the molecular mechanisms by which RES contributes to the treatment of KOA, utilizing a blend of bioinformatics approaches and experimental validation. First, gene expression profiles related to KOA were obtained from the GEO database. Subsequently, differential gene analysis was conducted on the samples, and modular genes linked to KOA were extracted through the application of a weighted gene co-expression network. The LASSO algorithm was utilized to identify crucial pathogenic genes in KOA, which were later confirmed using clinical samples. Targets for RES were sourced from traditional Chinese medicine databases, and the therapeutic targets for KOA treatment were determined by finding the intersection of these sources. An enrichment analysis was carried out based on the therapeutic targets identified. Molecular docking studies were conducted to further assess the binding affinity of key therapeutic genes with RES. Lastly, animal experiments were implemented to substantiate the molecular mechanisms by which RES acts in the treatment of KOA. We identified 460 module genes and 10 key predictive genes through LASSO analysis. The findings from the enrichment analysis concerning potential therapeutic targets for RES in the treatment of KOA reveal that the significant genes implicated include VEGFA, IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1. Subsequent validation with clinical samples revealed that IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1 were significantly elevated during the progression of KOA, while VEGFA was markedly reduced in the context of KOA. The outcomes of the GO and KEGG analyses suggest that the primary biological processes implicated encompass apoptosis, the FoxO signaling pathway, the IL-17 signaling pathway, cellular senescence, and the NF-κB signaling pathway. The findings from the immune infiltration analysis indicate that resting CD4 memory T cells, memory B cells, resting mast cells, eosinophils, and activated mast cells may have important functions in the immune mechanisms related to KOA. The results of animal experiments demonstrate that RES effectively inhibits the expression of inflammatory factors such as IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1 during the progression of KOA, promotes the expression of VEGFA, and concurrently suppresses the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, thereby reducing cartilage damage induced by MIA and delaying the progression of KOA. In summary, RES can regulate the expression of genes including VEGFA, IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1, inhibit the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, alleviate cartilage damage induced by MIA, and delay the progression of KOA.
papers.title_ko: 무릎 골관절염 치료에서 레스베라트롤의 기전 규명: 생물정보학과 실험적 검증

summary.question: 레스베라트롤이 무릎 골관절염에서 어떤 분자기전을 통해 작용하는지 확인하고자 하였다.
summary.methods: GEO 기반 유전자 분석, WGCNA와 LASSO로 핵심 유전자를 선별한 뒤 임상샘플, 분자도킹, 동물실험으로 검증한 연구이다.
summary.results: 레스베라트롤은 VEGFA를 증가시키고 IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, AKT1을 억제하며 FoxO 및 IL-17 신호경로를 낮춰 MIA 유발 연골손상을 줄이는 것으로 나타났다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 레스베라트롤의 KOA 관련 항염·항손상 기전을 시사하지만, 동물과 분자 수준 결과이므로 임상 적용은 추가 근거가 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 임상적 유효성은 직접 평가되지 않았고, 주로 생물정보학과 동물모델 결과에 근거한 점이 한계이다.

pico.p: 무릎 골관절염 환자 및 MIA 유발 동물모델
pico.o: 염증 관련 유전자 발현, 신호경로, 연골손상 및 질병 진행

papers.title: Sequential Stage-Specific Administration of Bushen-Tiaojing Decoctions II and III Ameliorates Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Ovarian Granulosa Cells of COH Mice by Regulating GRP75-Mediated MAM Homeostasis.
papers.authors: Ding X, Wen X, Xiong W, Liu H, Tang S, Li D et al.
papers.abstract:
Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) offers a distinct therapeutic approach to infertility. Bushen-Tiaojing Decoctions II (BSTJ-II-D) and III (BSTJ-III-D; collectively, BSTJD) are clinical formulas developed by Professor Huilan Du according to the TCM theory of stage-specific treatment and are widely used in the clinical management of infertility. Previous studies have shown that sequential, stage-specific administration of these formulas can improve mitochondrial energy metabolism and increase pregnancy rates among infertile women undergoing in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET). However, whether this sequential treatment improves mitochondrial function in ovarian granulosa cells (GCs) by preserving mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membrane (MAM) homeostasis remains unclear.
Glucose-regulated protein 75 (GRP75) is a key tethering protein that maintains MAM homeostasis. This study aimed to determine whether sequential, stage-specific administration of BSTJ-II-D and BSTJ-III-D ameliorates mitochondrial dysfunction in ovarian GCs by regulating GRP75-mediated MAM homeostasis.
A controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) mouse model was established, after which animals received BSTJ-II-D and BSTJ-III-D sequentially via oral gavage. A group treated with GRP75-IN-1, a novel small-molecule compound that targets and binds GRP75, was included as a control. MAM morphology, mitochondrial bioenergetic activity, and mitochondrial biogenesis were systematically evaluated. For the in vitro experiments, human KGN ovarian granulosa-like tumor cells were transduced with a GRP75-overexpressing lentiviral construct to clarify how elevated GRP75 expression affects MAM architecture and function and subsequently influences mitochondrial homeostasis. Protein levels of GRP75, voltage-dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU), sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ coactivator 1α (PGC-1α), and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) were assessed in GCs. Cellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, mitochondrial Ca2+ loading, and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) were determined using fluorescence-based assays. In addition, mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening was evaluated quantitatively by flow cytometric analysis.
Sequential BSTJD treatment attenuated COH-induced aberrant GRP75 overexpression, restored MAM ultrastructural integrity, reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress (OS) and Ca2+ overload, and enhanced mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis. Mechanistically, BSTJD increased the expression of SIRT1, PGC-1α, and Nrf2 while inhibiting activation of the PERK/ATF4 pathway, thereby alleviating endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and enhancing mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis. GRP75-IN-1 reproduced the protective effects of BSTJD. Conversely, GRP75 overexpression in KGN cells disrupted MAMs and impaired mitochondrial function, further supporting GRP75 as a key mediator of the protective effects of BSTJD.
Sequential BSTJD treatment preserves MAM homeostasis by suppressing aberrant GRP75 overexpression, thereby mitigating OS and mitochondrial Ca2+ overload. It also activates the SIRT1-PGC-1α-Nrf2 pathway to restore mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis, ultimately ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction in GCs. These findings provide new molecular evidence supporting the Bushen Tiaojing therapeutic approach for infertility.
papers.title_ko: 부신조경탕 II·III의 단계별 순차 투여가 GRP75 매개 MAM 항상성을 조절하여 COH 마우스 난포과립세포의 미토콘드리아 기능장애를 개선한다

summary.question: 부신조경탕 II·III의 순차적 단계별 투여가 GRP75 매개 MAM 항상성을 통해 난포과립세포의 미토콘드리아 기능장애를 개선하는지 평가하였다.
summary.methods: COH 마우스 모델과 KGN 세포 실험에서 부신조경탕 II·III, GRP75-IN-1, GRP75 과발현을 비교하며 MAM 구조와 미토콘드리아 기능 관련 지표를 분석하였다.
summary.results: 순차적 부신조경탕 치료는 GRP75 과발현, MAM 이상, 산화스트레스와 Ca2+ 과부하를 줄이고 SIRT1-PGC-1α-Nrf2 경로를 통해 미토콘드리아 에너지 대사와 생합성을 개선하였다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 단계별 한약 처방이 불임 관련 난소 미세환경에서 미토콘드리아 항상성에 관여할 가능성을 시사하지만, 동물·세포 수준 결과이므로 임상 적용은 추가 검증이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 마우스와 세포 기반 연구로 임상적 유효성과 안전성, 사람 대상 재현성은 명확하지 않다.

pico.o: MAM 항상성, 미토콘드리아 기능, 산화스트레스, Ca2+ 과부하

papers.title: Glycocalyx-binding and cell-penetrating peptide-modified nanomicelles for enhanced ocular delivery of quercetin and retinal protection in a dAMD model.
papers.authors: Li S, Yang Q, Zhu Y, Li T, Scherman D, Li W et al.
papers.abstract: Dry age-related macular degeneration (dAMD) is a highly prevalent degenerative retinal disease. Quercetin, a bioactive ingredient in traditional Chinese medicine, can mitigate the oxidative stress that helps drive dAMD; however, its low water solubility and poor corneal permeability limit its efficacy. We developed dual-functional polymeric micelles (PMs) co-conjugated with a glycocalyx-binding peptide (GBP) and a cell-penetrating peptide (TAT) for the enhanced topical ocular delivery of quercetin (QUE), named GT-PMs/QUE. The GT-PMs/QUE exhibited a particle size of 46.25 ± 3.05 nm and a zeta potential of -5.64 ± 0.92 mV. GT-PMs exhibited significantly higher cellular uptake efficiency than the unmodified group (PMs) and single-peptide modified groups (GBP-PMs and TAT-PMs). In the sodium iodate-induced oxidative damage model of adult retinal pigment epithelial cell line-19 (ARPE-19) cells, the GT-PMs/QUE treatment group showed significantly reduced ROS and MDA levels along with markedly increased SOD, CAT, and GSH activities that approached normal control levels compared to the model group. In a mouse model of dAMD, GT-PMs/QUE greatly improved the bioavailability of quercetin delivered via eye drop administration and attenuated sodium iodate-induced retinal damage. This study provides a theoretical and experimental basis for enhanced ocular delivery of quercetin and protection against dAMD-related retinal damage.
papers.title_ko: 글리코칼릭스 결합 및 세포침투 펩타이드로 개질한 나노미셀의 퀘르세틴 안구 전달 강화와 dAMD 모델에서의 망막 보호

summary.question: 퀘르세틴을 글리코칼릭스 결합 펩타이드와 세포침투 펩타이드로 개질한 나노미셀이 건성 연령관련 황반변성 모델에서 안구 전달과 망막 보호를 향상시키는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 퀘르세틴을 탑재한 이중 기능성 고분자 미셀을 제작해 ARPE-19 산화손상 모델과 나트륨 아이오데이트 유도 dAMD 마우스 모델에서 세포 흡수, 산화스트레스 지표, 약물 생체이용률, 망막 손상을 비교했다.
summary.results: GT-PMs/QUE는 미개질 미셀과 단일 펩타이드 미셀보다 세포 흡수가 높았고, ROS와 MDA를 낮추며 SOD, CAT, GSH를 증가시켰고, 마우스에서 점안 퀘르세틴의 생체이용률과 망막 보호 효과를 개선했다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 전임상 자료로서 퀘르세틴의 국소 안구 전달을 개선하는 제형 전략이 dAMD 관련 산화손상 완화에 도움이 될 가능성을 시사한다.
summary.limitations: 세포와 동물 모델 기반 연구이므로 실제 환자에서의 유효성과 안전성은 확인되지 않았다.

papers.title: Acupuncture Attenuates Myopia Progression by Suppressing Scleral Inflammation and Enhancing Neurotrophic Signaling.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zhou Y, Wang Y, Xu W, Shangguan Y, Li B et al.
papers.abstract: Myopia is a common ocular disorder characterized by excessive axial elongation, and effective strategies for limiting its progression remain limited. This study investigated whether acupuncture attenuates myopia progression in a guinea pig model of form-deprivation myopia and examined the involvement of scleral inflammation and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-mediated neurotrophic signaling. Guinea pigs were randomly assigned to control, myopia, acupuncture-only, and myopia plus acupuncture groups for phenotypic evaluation. Additional sham acupuncture and myopia-plus-acupuncture groups, combined with subconjunctival cyclotraxin B (CTX-B) administration, were included to evaluate acupuncture specificity and the involvement of BDNF/tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) signaling. Following intervention, refractive error and axial length were measured in the primary treatment groups. Scleral remodeling markers, including collagen type I alpha 1 (COL1A1) and α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA); inflammatory mediators, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB); and neurotrophic factors, including BDNF, TrkB, nerve growth factor, and neurotrophin-4, were evaluated using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, quantitative reverse transcription PCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Acupuncture was associated with reduced myopic refractive shifts and axial elongation. At the final observation time point, axial elongation was lower in the myopia plus acupuncture group than in the myopia group (ΔAL, 0.77 ± 0.19 mm vs. 1.42 ± 0.20 mm; Cohen's d = 1.51). Acupuncture also reduced scleral IL-1β, IL-6, and NF-κB expression and increased BDNF, TrkB, nerve growth factor, and neurotrophin-4 expression. Sham acupuncture showed limited effects on these molecular changes, whereas CTX-B attenuated acupuncture-associated alterations in BDNF/TrkB signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, and inflammatory markers. These findings suggest that acupuncture attenuates myopia progression through coordinated regulation of scleral inflammation and neurotrophic support involving BDNF/TrkB signaling.
papers.title_ko: 침술은 공막 염증 억제와 신경영양 신호 강화로 근시 진행을 완화한다

summary.question: 침술이 형태박탈 근시 모델에서 근시 진행을 완화하는지와 그 기전이 공막 염증 및 BDNF/TrkB 신호와 관련되는지를 평가하였다.
summary.methods: 형태박탈 근시 기니피그 모델에서 대조군, 근시군, 침술군 등을 비교하고, 가짜침과 CTX-B를 이용해 침술 특이성과 BDNF/TrkB 관여를 검증한 동물실험이다.
summary.results: 침술은 굴절이상과 안구축 연장을 감소시켰고, 공막의 염증 표지자는 낮추며 BDNF/TrkB 관련 신경영양 표지자는 높였고, CTX-B는 이러한 효과를 일부 상쇄하였다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 침술이 근시 진행 관련 생물학적 경로에 영향을 줄 가능성을 시사하지만, 동물실험 결과이므로 임상 적용 가능성은 추가 연구로 확인이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 기니피그 동물모델 연구여서 사람 근시 환자에게의 일반화에는 제한이 있다.

pico.o: 굴절이상, 안구축 연장, 공막 염증 및 BDNF/TrkB 관련 표지자

papers.title: Evaluating Macrophage Polarization and Inflammation in Bitongqing-Treated Collagen-Induced Arthritis Rats.
papers.authors: Pan J, Zhu W, Liu C, Wu Y, Zhao J, Wang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and immune dysregulation. Traditional Chinese medicine formulas such as Bitongqing Decoction (BTQ) are used clinically, but reproducible workflows are needed to characterize their absorbed constituents and associated immunological effects. This article presents an integrated protocol comprising herbal preparation, collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) induction, 21-day oral treatment, serum ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS), arthritis scoring, micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), hematoxylin and eosin staining, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and western blotting. The workflow evaluates macroscopic disease manifestations, joint pathology, inflammatory mediators, macrophage-associated M1-like and M2-like markers, splenic T helper 1 (Th1)- and regulatory T cell (Treg)-associated markers, and NF-κB/MAPK signaling proteins. Representative data showed that BTQ treatment was associated with improved arthritis-related outcomes, lower levels of inflammatory mediators, reduced CD80, iNOS, MHCII, and STAT1 signaling, increased CD163 and ARG-1 signaling, altered CXCR3 and FOXP3 signaling, and reduced phosphorylation of P65, ERK, and JNK. Because marker intensities, rather than cell-number ratios, were measured, these findings are described as changes in marker profiles rather than as direct measurements of M1/M2 or Th1/Treg balance. This protocol provides a multimodal framework for pharmacological studies of complex herbal formulas by linking the characterization of circulating constituents with structural, histological, and immunological readouts while preserving physiological interactions among synovial macrophages, lymphocytes, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, and other joint-resident cells.
papers.title_ko: 콜라겐 유도 관절염 랫드에서 비통청의 대식세포 극화와 염증 평가

summary.question: 비통청(BTQ) 처치가 콜라겐 유도 관절염 랫드의 염증과 면역 표지자에 어떤 변화를 보이는지 평가하고자 하였다.
summary.methods: 콜라겐 유도 관절염 랫드에 21일간 경구 BTQ를 투여하고, UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS, 관절 점수, micro-CT, 조직염색, 면역염색, ELISA, western blot으로 병리와 면역 표지자를 분석한 프로토콜 연구이다.
summary.results: 대표 자료에서 BTQ는 관절염 관련 지표와 염증 매개체를 낮추고 CD80, iNOS, MHCII, STAT1 및 p-P65, p-ERK, p-JNK를 감소시키며 CD163, ARG-1과 일부 CXCR3, FOXP3 관련 신호를 증가시켰다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 복합 한약 처방의 전임상 약리평가에서 순환 성분 분석과 구조·조직·면역 지표를 함께 보는 다중모달 접근이 유용할 수 있다.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine as Adjunctive Care in Cancer and Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Narrative Review of Shared Frameworks and Evidence Gaps.
papers.authors: Li B, Xu X
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has increasingly been investigated as an adjunctive approach to conventional treatment in chronic and complex diseases, including cancer and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Although cancer and RA differ substantially in pathogenesis and therapeutic goals, both are associated with persistent symptom burden, treatment-related adverse effects, impaired physical function, psychological distress, and long-term supportive-care needs. This narrative review evaluates TCM within this shared adjunctive-care framework while maintaining disease-specific interpretation of the available evidence. In cancer, TCM-related interventions have been investigated for supportive symptom management, pain relief, treatment tolerance, quality-of-life improvement, and potential modulation of biological processes, including apoptosis, angiogenesis, immune regulation, invasion, metastasis, and multidrug resistance. In RA, Chinese herbal medicines, acupuncture, and related approaches have been evaluated for their potential effects on pain, inflammation, physical function, bone remodeling, and early disease-related processes. TCM-related mind-body practices, such as qigong and tai chi, may also provide psychological support, whereas mindfulness-based interventions are considered supportive-care strategies rather than TCM interventions. Current evidence ranges from mechanistic and preclinical studies to observational studies, single-arm clinical studies, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses, with substantial variation in methodological quality. Overall, TCM should be considered a potential complement to, rather than a replacement for, established oncological or rheumatological treatment. Further well-designed clinical studies, standardized interventions, rigorous quality control, safety monitoring, and clinically meaningful outcome assessment are required to define its appropriate role in multidisciplinary care.

papers.title: Scientific Frontiers and Emerging Themes in Acupuncture for Stroke: A Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.authors: Chu Y, Ma L, Gao Y, Chen J, Chen Y, Chen Y
papers.abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of death and long-term disability worldwide, and acupuncture is widely used as a complementary therapy in stroke rehabilitation. However, the rapidly expanding and heterogeneous literature lacks systematic knowledge structure analysis and identification of emerging frontiers. This study retrieved publications related to acupuncture for stroke from the Web of Science Core Collection published from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2025, and applied bibliometric tools including CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Scimago Graphica to visualize publication output, collaboration networks (countries, institutions, authors), co-citation patterns, journal dual-map overlays, and keyword bursts, with the aim of delineating research hotspots and developmental trends. The results show a steady increase in annual publication output, with China, the United States, and South Korea being the most productive countries. Core research teams have been established, but cross-regional cooperation still requires strengthening. Co-citation analysis revealed classic clusters focusing on neuroplasticity, inflammatory regulation, and mechanisms of electroacupuncture. Keyword burst detection indicates that early studies centered on motor recovery and acupuncture techniques, whereas recent frontiers have shifted towards "neuroprotection", "oxidative stress", "default mode network", and "neurorehabilitation guidelines". Research hotspots are shifting from purely evaluating clinical efficacy toward multimodal mechanistic exploration and integration with evidence-based recommendations. In conclusion, the field of acupuncture for stroke is in a phase of rapid development, with the research focus shifting from basic efficacy validation to deeper mechanistic understanding and interdisciplinary integration. The knowledge maps provided in this study can help researchers quickly identify frontiers and inform future clinical trial design and guideline development.

papers.title: From Mechanistic Evidence to Clinical Translation: A Narrative Review of Chinese Herbal Medicine for Insomnia.
papers.authors: Li X, Xu H, Zhang Y, Lu J, Zhang Y, Zhang L et al.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders and a major public health problem worldwide. Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) is widely used as a complementary and alternative approach for chronic insomnia. Clinical studies have reported preliminary evidence of benefit for Chinese herbal formulas, whereas mechanistic research has examined single herbs, extracts, active constituents, and compound formulas using multi-omics analysis, network pharmacology, molecular prediction, and experimental validation. However, clinical studies are typically small and of inconsistent methodological quality, with limited long-term follow-up, while mechanistic evidence remains fragmented and lacks systematic integration and translational validation. These limitations restrict the development of CHM interventions from experimental evidence to clinically testable interventions for insomnia. This narrative review evaluates existing research across five translational dimensions, namely chemical characterization and preparation quality, exposure and pharmacodynamic evidence, mechanism and target validation, sleep-related clinical endpoints, and safety. It aims to clarify the current state of research on CHM interventions for insomnia and to identify key limitations and priorities for future research. Most available evidence comes from preclinical studies, which suggest that CHM may influence sleep-related processes through γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and serotonergic signaling, the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis-autophagy balance, and the brain-gut-microbiota axis. Much of this evidence reflects changes in biochemical markers or pathway activity, while only a few studies directly test target function. Clinical studies provide preliminary evidence of short-term improvements in subjective sleep outcomes. However, clinical translation remains limited by insufficient evidence for objective sleep improvement and long-term efficacy and safety. Future work should carry a few well-characterized interventions through the full evidence chain, prioritizing standardized preparations, exposure and pharmacodynamic assessment, objective sleep endpoints, long-term follow-up, and safety.

papers.title: Moxibustion Regulates the Imbalance of Cartilage Degradation and Repair in Knee Osteoarthritis Rabbits via the SDF-1/CXCR4 Axis: Is Stimulating Heat-Sensitized Acupoints More Efficacious?
papers.authors: Li L, Chen R, Zhang Y, Hu L, Qiu Y, Yan C et al.
papers.abstract:
This study investigated whether moxibustion, particularly at heat-sensitized acupoints, exerts therapeutic effects on knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and whether these effects are associated with the modulation of the SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling axis, a key regulator of cartilage metabolism.
A KOA model was induced in rabbits, which were then randomized into control (n=6), model (n=6), and moxibustion groups. Following a 14-day moxibustion intervention, the moxibustion group was further classified into heat-sensitive moxibustion (HSM, n=6) and non-heat-sensitive moxibustion (NSM, n=6) subgroups based on thermal response measured by infrared thermal imaging. Heat-sensitization was defined as a sustained distal skin temperature elevation ≥ 1°C during treatment, while non-heat-sensitive was defined as an elevation < 1°C. After a 14-day intervention, outcomes were assessed via the Lequesne MG index, histopathology, RT-qPCR, Western blot, and Micro-CT.
Compared to the model group (Lequesne score: 9.667±1.633), both HSM (3.167±0.753, p<0.01) and NSM (5.000±0.894, p<0.01) significantly improved joint function. HSM significantly outperformed NSM (p<0.05). At the molecular level, HSM significantly downregulated SDF-1 (1.570±0.131 vs 1.957±0.301, p<0.05), CXCR4 (1.902±0.318 vs 2.313±0.277, p<0.05), and MMP-13 (2.166±0.312 vs 2.608±0.340, p<0.05) mRNA expression, while significantly upregulating SOX9 (0.774±0.086 vs 0.638±0.089, p<0.05) and Col2a1 (0.728±0.091 vs 0.601±0.078, p<0.05) compared to NSM. In terms of subchondral bone, although both moxibustion groups showed significant improvements over the model group (all p<0.05), no statistically significant differences were observed between HSM and NSM for BMD, BV/TV, Tb.N, Tb.Th, or Tb.Sp (all p>0.05).
Moxibustion ameliorates KOA, and this effect is accompanied by the suppression of the SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling axis and restoration of the balance between cartilage catabolism and anabolism. Stimulation of heat-sensitized acupoints offers superior benefits for functional recovery and molecular markers of cartilage repair compared to non-heat-sensitive acupoints, although this advantage was not observed in subchondral bone parameters.

papers.title: Impact of climate change on Chinese medicinal plants and adaptation strategies.
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.authors: Yuan W, Gu M, Liu D, Liu Q, Sun Q, Zeng X
papers.abstract:
Global climate change threats to plant communities worldwide. This review explicitly narrows its scope exclusively to Chinese medicine plants (CMPs), the core raw materials for Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). CMPs are distinguished by clinical efficacy dependent on complex secondary‑metabolite mixtures, geo‑authentic (Daodi) production systems, and large‑scale industrial supply chains. Existing studies remain fragmented, most studies examine single‑factor stress, whereas few systematically link ecological shifts, phytochemical disturbance, clinical therapeutic performance, and industrial supply‑chain risks. This review synthesizes multi‑source evidence to unpack climate‑driven impacts on CMPs, highlights unresolved research limitations, and proposes tiered, evidence‑informed adaptation pathways, while explicitly distinguishing theoretical proposals, laboratory‑validated approaches and field‑proven practical solutions.
We synthesized published field surveys, controlled physiological experiments, species‑distribution modelling outputs, and post‑harvest quality assessments. Impacts were organized across three dimensions of ecological adaptability (habitat shift, population decline), phytochemical disruption (shifts in secondary-metabolism profiles), and industrial‑clinical consequences (supply volatility, altered therapeutic potency). We systematically evaluated study limitations, inconsistent empirical observations, and translational gaps between laboratory results and real‑world field conditions, and marked whether quantitative data originated from field measurement, controlled experiment or model simulation.
Climate warming drives poleward and uphill habitat shifts for many CMP species, compressing suitable niches for geo‑authentic endemic taxa and exacerbating wild‑resource scarcity. Combined stressors (temperature anomalies, erratic precipitation, elevated CO2 and intensified pest pressure) jointly disrupt secondary-metabolite regulatory networks, altering absolute concentrations and proportional balances of bioactive constituents. Under combined heat‑humidity exposure, toxic metabolites may accumulate. These cascading effects translate into reduced yield, market price volatility, potential shifts in therapeutic activity inferred from phytochemical alteration, elevated pesticide-residue risks, and shortened post-harvest shelf-life. Key unresolved gaps include insufficient long‑term coupled ecological‑pharmacological-postharvest monitoring, poorly characterized multi‑stressor interaction mechanisms, absence of climate‑adjusted herbal quality benchmarks, and under-recognized post-harvest quality risk amplified by extreme weather. Notably, many proposed adaptation interventions are only validated under laboratory conditions, or are transferred from conventional crop systems, and lack large‑scale field demonstration; conflicting experimental outcomes across different species and test conditions also constrain generalizable conclusions CONCLUSION: Climate change modifies CMP phytochemical composition and may thereby influence clinical value via interconnected pre‑harvest and post‑harvest mechanistic chains; direct evidence linking such phytochemical shifts to altered therapeutic outcomes remains limited. A suite of promising strategies exists, including climate-informed wild-germplasm conservation, stress-resistant molecular breeding, precision ecological cultivation, multi-indicator long-term surveillance, standardized post-harvest processing, and cross‑jurisdictional cooperation. Nevertheless, most of these measures have not been broadly implemented. Interdisciplinary frameworks integrating climatology, plant pharmacology, agronomy, and herbal industrial processing are required to build climate‑resilient TCM supply chains and help maintain consistent therapeutic outcomes, pending further empirical validation linking phytochemical shifts to clinical performance, for public‑health purposes.

papers.authors: Chen X, Yang L, Li J, Zhao L, Yu Q, Yan X et al.
papers.abstract:
Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with nonsmokers comprising a notable proportion of cases. The complexity of its molecular pathogenesis poses substantial challenges for the development of effective therapeutic strategies. Traditional Chinese medicine-derived compounds have garnered attention for their multi-target engagement and favorable safety profiles.
This study aimed to characterize the antitumor effects and elucidate the mechanistic basis of 11-oxo-mogroside V, a bioactive triterpenoid saponin from Siraitia grosvenorii, in LUAD.
In vitro assays (CCK-8, flow cytometry, wound-healing, metabolic measurements) were performed on lung adenocarcinoma cells. In vivo efficacy was evaluated using a xenograft mouse model with bioluminescent monitoring and TUNEL staining. Transcriptomic profiling, molecular docking, immunoblotting, and co-immunoprecipitation elucidated mechanistic pathways.
11-oxo-mogroside V (800 μg/mL, 72 h) significantly reduced cell viability, induced G0/G1 arrest, and promoted apoptosis (apoptotic rate increased from 3.01% to 12.00%, P < 0.0001). Migration was suppressed (wound closure reduced from 77.66% to 43.98%, P < 0.0001). Metabolic disruption was evidenced by decreased intracellular ATP, glucose uptake, and LDH activity. In vivo, 11-oxo-mogroside V (100 mg/kg, daily) markedly inhibited tumor growth (photon flux reduced from 2.65 × 10¹⁰ to 1.50 × 10¹⁰, P < 0.0001) and increased apoptosis (TUNEL-positive cells from 0.40% to 5.97%, P < 0.0001). Mechanistically, RNA-seq analysis and molecular docking suggested TGFB2, HDAC1, and c-Myc as potential molecular targets, with docking simulations indicating favorable binding affinities. Western blot confirmed downregulation of TGFB2, Smad2/3, TGIF, HDAC1, c-Myc, and Bcl2, alongside upregulation of Bax, with co-IP demonstrating HDAC1-TGIF1 interaction.
11-oxo-mogroside V exerts potent anti-LUAD activity by disrupting metabolic homeostasis and suppressing TGFβ2/HDAC1/c-Myc signaling, positioning it as a promising lead compound for therapeutic development.

papers.title: Molecular mechanism of Xanthotoxol against gastric cancer: A comprehensive study integrating network pharmacology, computer simulations, and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Yang Y, Du YH, Song C, Ma LN, Luo L, Xu DX et al.
papers.abstract:
Gastric cancer (GC) is a prevalent malignant tumor of the digestive system worldwide. Xanthotoxol (Xan), a natural compound extracted from traditional Chinese medicine such as Angelica archangelica, has demonstrated antitumor properties. However, its specific effects on GC remain unreported.
Hub targets of Xan in GC were identified by integrating weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) with network pharmacology. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted to analyze the interaction between the hub targets and Xan. The effects of Xan on GC cell proliferation, cell cycle, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were examined using cell experiments and xenograft tumor model. Histopathological evaluation of changes in tumor and liver tissues was performed after Xan intervention. Western blot and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were employed to analyze hub target expression and clarify Xan's molecular mechanism against GC.
A total of six hub genes highly correlated with GC were identified (MMP12, KDR, CCND1, PDGFRB, PLAU, and PLK1). Molecular docking and MD simulations revealed a significant binding affinity between Xan and hub genes. Experiments demonstrated that Xan inhibited proliferation, cell cycle, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. Xan could alleviate liver injury caused by subcutaneous tumor in mice. Furthermore, Xan upregulated MMP12 expression and downregulated KDR, CCND1, PDGFRB, PLAU, and PLK1 in GC cells.
Xan shows promise as a GC treatment by modulating MMP12, KDR, CCND1, PDGFRB, PLAU, and PLK1 expression, which inhibits proliferation, cell cycle, migration, and invasion, while enhancing apoptosis and reducing liver damage.

papers.title: [Hiccups in adults: Pathophysiology, diagnostic approach, and management].
papers.authors: Aubignat M
papers.abstract: Chronic hiccups, defined as lasting more than 48hours, represent an underestimated clinical entity with potentially severe impacts on patients' quality of life. The pathophysiology involves a reflex arc comprising the phrenic and vagus nerves, integrated at the pontomedullary level. Recent advances highlight the role of a central pattern generator and neurotransmitter systems (GABA, dopamine, serotonin) in the genesis and perpetuation of hiccups. Epidemiological data reveal a striking male predominance (82-92% of cases), with an organic cause identified in over 90% of men. Etiologies are dominated by gastrointestinal causes, particularly gastroesophageal reflux disease (up to 80% of cases), followed by central neurological causes including Wallenberg syndrome. The diagnostic approach relies on targeted history and physical examination, complemented by laboratory tests, chest radiography, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, and brain imaging when clinically indicated. Therapeutic management follows a stepwise approach: etiological treatment, proton pump inhibitors as first-line therapy, followed by baclofen or gabapentin. Refractory cases may require neuroleptics or interventional techniques (phrenic nerve block, acupuncture). Despite the absence of formal guidelines, this review proposes a pragmatic diagnostic and therapeutic algorithm based on current literature evidence.

papers.title: Assessing Chiropractic, Complementary and Integrative Health, and Whole Health Services Utilization Among a Cohort of Pregnant and Postpartum Veterans.
papers.journal: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health
papers.authors: Muller RD, Wallace KF, Mattocks KM, Lisi AJ, Heapy AA, Kroll-Desrosiers A et al.
papers.abstract:
Musculoskeletal (MSK) pain is common among women veterans and may be exacerbated during pregnancy and postpartum. However, little is known regarding pregnant veterans' engagement with chiropractic, complementary and integrative health (CIH), and Whole Health (e.g., health and wellness coaching) services in this population.
Pregnant and postpartum veterans were identified from a longitudinal, prospective, multisite cohort study. Demographic and clinical characteristics were collected via Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) electronic health record and study survey data. Visits to VA-funded chiropractic, CIH, and Whole Health services during pregnancy, the first 9 postpartum months, and the 5 years preceding pregnancy were identified. We described participants' engagement with these services and assessed factors associated with use of any of these services during pregnancy and/or postpartum using logistic regression.
Of the 1,139 veterans included, 109 (10%) engaged with chiropractic, CIH, and/or Whole Health services during pregnancy and/or postpartum. Chiropractic (53%), acupuncture (20%), and massage therapy (10%) were the most used services. Visits to services were similar between pregnant (54%) and postpartum (46%) timeframes. Engagement with these services in the 5 years preceding pregnancy (odds ratio [OR]: 6.90; 95% confidence interval [CI] [4.24, 11.25]) and presence of a mental health diagnosis (anxiety, depression, and/or posttraumatic stress disorder) (OR: 1.79; 95% CI [1.02, 3.17]) were significantly associated with chiropractic, CIH, and/or Whole Health service use during pregnancy and/or postpartum. All other demographic and clinical variables were nonsignificant.
Results from this study may inform future implementation and administrative investigations of pregnant and postpartum veterans' use of chiropractic, CIH, and Whole Health services.

papers.title: Wendan Decoction-Derived TMF Alleviates Endolymphatic Hydrops by Modulating the DUSP3/p38 MAPK/AQP2 Axis.
papers.authors: Xia J, Huang J, Hou X, Hua H, Chen M
papers.abstract:
Wendan Decoction is a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula historically used for phlegm-related dizziness and vertigo. Recent studies have shown that Wendan Decoction can ameliorate experimental endolymphatic hydrops (EH), a characteristic pathological correlate of Ménière's disease. However, the bioactive constituents responsible for these effects and their molecular targets remain incompletely defined.
This study aimed to identify and quantify a pharmacologically relevant constituent of Wendan Decoction and to investigate its molecular target and mechanism of action in experimental EH.
Candidate constituents and regulatory targets were prioritized through ADME-guided screening, target prediction, MD-associated transcriptomic analysis, protein-protein interaction network analysis, pathway enrichment, MAPK pathway mapping, and molecular docking. Targeted UPLC-ESI-MS/MS was used to verify and quantify 5,6,7,4'-tetramethoxyflavone (TMF) in Wendan Decoction granules. The interaction between TMF and DUSP3 was examined using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and a cell lysate-based cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). The effects of TMF were evaluated in LPS-stimulated HEI-OC1 cells and a DDAVP-induced guinea pig model of EH. DUSP3 knockdown and pharmacological inhibition of p38 MAPK with SB203580 were used to investigate the functional relationships among DUSP3, p38 MAPK, AQP2, and ZO-1.
TMF was detected in Wendan Decoction granules at 0.0379% (w/w). SPR showed micromolar binding between TMF and recombinant DUSP3, while CETSA showed that TMF increased the thermal stability of DUSP3. In LPS-stimulated HEI-OC1 cells, TMF reduced inflammatory mediator production, increased DUSP3 and ZO-1 expression, inhibited p38 MAPK activation, and decreased AQP2 expression. SB203580 attenuated AQP2 upregulation, ZO-1 reduction, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production, including after DUSP3 silencing, supporting p38 MAPK as a downstream component of DUSP3-associated signaling. In DDAVP-treated guinea pigs, TMF reduced morphometrically quantified cochlear hydrops, alleviated cochlear ultrastructural injury and vestibular-associated behavioral impairment, and decreased cochlear inflammatory cytokine levels. Cochlear DUSP3 knockdown was confirmed at both the mRNA and protein levels and partially weakened TMF-mediated regulation of the p38 MAPK/AQP2 axis.
TMF is a quantified Wendan Decoction-derived constituent with protective activity against experimental EH. The findings support a direct interaction between TMF and DUSP3 and suggest that TMF alleviates EH-associated pathological changes, at least in part, through DUSP3-associated regulation of p38 MAPK activation and downstream AQP2 and ZO-1 expression.

papers.title: Jian'er Jiedu granule alleviates acute lung injury via NOD2/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis: Network pharmacology, machine learning, and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Yang L, Wang X, Guo Y, Niu Z, Liu C, Hong J et al.
papers.abstract:
Acute lung injury (ALI) is a severe inflammatory disorder associated with high mortality. Jian'er Jiedu granule (JEJD), a formulation developed by Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, has shown promise in alleviating Omicron-related symptoms; however, its therapeutic effects on ALI remain unclear.
To explore the therapeutic effects and mechanisms of action of JEJD in ALI.
The active components and potential targets of JEJD were screened using TCMSP, TCMIP, TCMID, and Herb databases. ALI-related genes were obtained from GeneCards, OMIM, and Disgenet databases. The final candidate genes were determined using a combination of machine learning algorithms, cross-species gene expression analysis, and assessment of clinical diagnostic relevance. The relationship between JEJD, ALI, and the identified genes was further analyzed using functional enrichment analysis, competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory network analysis, single-cell transcriptomic data analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation validation. Finally, an ALI mouse model was established via intratracheal LPS instillation to investigate the effects of JEJD in vivo, and in vitro experiments using MH-S macrophages were performed to validate the anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
Forty-nine intersection genes were identified using database analysis. Machine learning algorithms combined with protein-protein interaction network analysis screened VCAM1 and CASP1 as candidate genes. Enrichment analysis indicated that these genes functioned as downstream components of the NOD-like receptor signaling pathway. Animal experiments showed JEJD significantly reduced the protein levels of NOD2, p-NF-κB, NLRP3, VCAM1, and Caspase-1, thereby alleviating LPS-induced ALI.
By integrating network pharmacology, machine learning, and experimental validation, we demonstrated that JEJD alleviates ALI at least partly through the NOD2/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling axis, with VCAM1 and Caspase-1 functioning as critical downstream effector molecules. These findings highlight the therapeutic potential of JEJD in regulating inflammatory networks.

papers.title: Multi‑target mechanisms of paeoniflorin in inflammatory regulation: A network pharmacology (Review).
papers.authors: Zhang J, Ye J, Jin K, Sun X, Yu X, Zhao Y et al.
papers.abstract: Paeoniflorin (PF), a monoterpene glycoside from Paeonia roots, shows low toxicity and broad anti‑inflammatory activity. A systematic review (PubMed, through 2025) with network pharmacology indicates that PF restores mitochondrial function, raises anti‑inflammatory mediators (IL‑10 and arginase‑1), reduces TNF‑α, IL‑1β and IL‑6, and eases oxidative stress. Its effects hinge on intertwined routes, dampening TLR4/MyD88, blocking NF‑κB nuclear entry, lowering MAPK phosphorylation, reshaping JAK‑STAT, and disrupting NLRP3 inflammasome assembly. Network mapping singles out a conserved core module (MAPK1, MAPK3, HSP90AA1, TP53, ESR1, BCL2, HIF1A, IL6, IL10 and FGF2), with HSP90AA1 and ESR1 as disease‑tailored effectors in rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis (OA). PF absorbs fast and gathers in the liver with minimal toxicity, yet oral availability stays poor. Preclinical promise spans OA, colitis, and atherosclerosis, while clinical data remain thin. Synergistic pairing with other agents and structural refinement of PF broaden its reach, though such computational leads need experimental corroboration. Future efforts should improve its bioavailability, develop targeted delivery systems, and conduct rigorous clinical trials to move PF from tradition to evidence‑based medicine.

papers.title: Associations between lifestyle behaviors and traditional Chinese Medicine body constitutions: A cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Tsai CI, Chen YM, Tseng JS, Fu PK, Wang JS, Wang JL et al.
papers.abstract: This study aims to assess the associations between lifestyle behaviors - including smoking, alcohol consumption, tea consumption, and leisure-time physical activity - and traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) body constitutions (BCs), Yin deficiency, Yang deficiency, and phlegm stasis, among Taiwanese adults participating in the Taiwan Biobank Study. A total of 15,665 participants from the Taiwan Biobank Study were included in the analysis. Comprehensive data were collected on lifestyle behaviors (including smoking, alcohol consumption, tea consumption, and leisure-time physical activity) and family medical history. TCM BC types - Yin deficiency, Yang deficiency, and phlegm stasis - were assessed using a well-validated BC questionnaire. Associations between lifestyle behaviors and BC types were examined using multivariate logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs). The average age was 46.55 years (standard deviation: 12.17), with 5611 males (35.82%). Compared with nonsmokers, current smokers had a significantly higher likelihood of having Yang deficiency (OR [95% confidence interval (CI)]: 1.62 [1.39-1.89]), Yin deficiency (1.64 [1.41-1.90]), and phlegm stasis (1.88 [1.59-2.22]) after multivariate adjustment. Compared with nondrinkers, current drinkers had a significantly higher likelihood of having Yin deficiency (1.21 [1.02-1.44]) and phlegm stasis (1.27 [1.04-1.56]) after multivariate adjustment. Tea consumption was significantly associated with phlegm stasis (1.18 [1.08-1.29]). Regarding leisure-time physical activity, this habit was negatively associated with Yang deficiency, Yin deficiency, and phlegm stasis with multivariate adjustment (0.71 [0.65-0.78], 0.74 [0.68-0.81], and 0.63 [0.58-0.70], respectively). This study demonstrates that lifestyle behaviors are associated with imbalanced TCM BCs, particularly Yin deficiency, Yang deficiency, and phlegm stasis.
